headline: Insurance drag offsets growth at pipelines and hotels
summary_short: Loews' Q1 2026 net income fell 8.9% y/y to $337M ($1.63 diluted EPS, -6.3% y/y) as revenue rose 1.4% y/y to $4,555M; the decline was driven by weaker CNA underwriting and unfavorable prior-year reserve development, partly offset by gains at Loews Hotels and Boardwalk Pipelines.
summary_long: Net income attributable to Loews fell 8.9% y/y to $337M ($1.63 diluted EPS) as CNA's underwriting results weakened -- the Property & Casualty combined ratio rose to 102.2% from 98.4% on $100M of unfavorable prior-year reserve development (mainly E&O and general liability), and CNA's core income fell to $225M from $281M, partly offset by higher net investment income. Boardwalk Pipelines' net income rose to $159M (+4.6%) on higher contracting rates and utilization, while Loews Hotels & Co swung from breakeven to $26M on higher Universal Orlando joint-venture income. Operating cash flow fell to $72M from $736M y/y on reinsurance-treaty payment timing. Loews repurchased $31M of stock and paid a $0.0625/share dividend; shareholders' equity rose to $18,704M.

drivers.explanation: Net income fell as weaker CNA underwriting and unfavorable prior-year reserve development outweighed growth at Boardwalk Pipelines and Loews Hotels & Co, the latter swinging from breakeven to $26M on Universal Orlando joint-venture gains.

Growth was driven by higher Boardwalk Pipelines transportation, storage and NGL revenues on higher contracting rates and utilization, and higher CNA insurance premiums, partly offset by lower ethane product sales and lower hotel non-insurance warranty revenue.

Decline was primarily driven by lower net income at CNA (weaker underlying underwriting results and unfavorable net prior year loss reserve development) and lower parent-company results, partially offset by higher net income at Loews Hotels & Co and Boardwalk Pipelines.

Decline reflects reinsurance-treaty payments made in Q1 2026 that were instead paid in Q2 2025 last year, plus higher net claim payments at CNA, partly offset by higher investment earnings.
Increase was driven by Boardwalk Pipelines, where capex rose to $144M from $52M as growth-project spending increased to $110M from $16M.
Parent-company cash and investments rose to $4.5B from $3.9B on $691M of dividends and distributions received from CNA (including a $497M special dividend) and Boardwalk Pipelines.
Growth reflects retained earnings, partly offset by a swing to $251M of other comprehensive loss (mainly unrealized fixed-maturity securities losses) and $31M of share buybacks.
Share count fell on continued buybacks -- Loews repurchased 0.3 million shares for $31M this quarter versus 4.5 million shares for $380M a year ago.
